0.text:
The process begins with sending the contract to the client.

Once the contract is sent, three activities are performed simultaneously: future calls are scheduled, the client's CRM is updated, and the project management profile is updated.

After scheduling future calls, the process continues with one or both of the following paths: getting approval for the first draft, or creating a first draft of the marketing plan. If the first draft of the marketing plan is created, campaign ideas are then researched. These paths converge once the selected activities are completed.

Meanwhile, after updating the project management profile, the questionnaire completion is confirmed.

The process waits until all parallel branches are complete: the client's CRM has been updated, the questionnaire is confirmed complete, and the approval/marketing plan activities have finished. Only then does the process proceed to inform the client of the project start.

Following this notification, three activities occur in parallel: changes are made based on a follow-up call, a follow-up call is held, and a post-onboarding survey is sent.

Once all three of these activities are completed, the process ends.

The process begins at the start event and proceeds with confirming the basic information. Following this, the performance of the process is assessed.

At this point, multiple activities can be performed in any combination: considering where bottlenecks occur, looking to see if the process can be simplified, and defining how long it takes to complete the process.

When looking at process simplification, additional analysis activities may follow: examining potentially wasteful steps and assessing if any steps are confusing. These examination activities can be performed in any combination and then converge together.

Once all the parallel analysis streams are complete—the bottleneck consideration, the simplification analysis with its sub-activities, and the time definition—the paths merge and the potential process improvements are written.

After documenting the improvements, approval for the processing improvements is obtained. Once approved, two activities can proceed in any combination: adding feedback on the updated process and updating the process documents. These activities then converge.

Following this convergence, three activities can be undertaken in any combination: scheduling the next process review and optimization, determining how the process will be monitored, and communicating the process changes. The communication of process changes leads directly to implementing the process changes.

Once the scheduling, monitoring determination, and implementation are all complete, the paths merge and the process concludes at the end event.

The process begins with confirming the basic information, followed by assessing the performance of the process.

After the performance assessment, multiple activities can be performed in parallel or selectively: considering where bottlenecks occur, looking to see if the process can be simplified, and defining how long it takes to complete the process.

When looking at simplification opportunities, this leads to further parallel analysis where potentially wasteful steps are examined and an assessment is made to determine if any steps are confusing. These two examination activities converge once completed.

Once all the analysis paths are complete—whether examining bottlenecks, assessing wasteful or confusing steps, or defining process duration—the findings are consolidated and potential process improvements are written.

The proposed improvements are then submitted to get approval for processing improvements.

Upon receiving approval, two activities can proceed in parallel or selectively: adding feedback on the updated process and updating the process documents. These activities are synchronized once finished.

Following the documentation updates, three activities can occur in parallel or selectively: scheduling the next process review and optimization, determining how the process will be monitored, and communicating the process changes. The communication of changes leads directly to implementing the process changes.

Once the next review is scheduled, the monitoring approach is determined, and the process changes are implemented, all paths converge and the process comes to an end.

The process begins when payment confirmation is needed. First, the payment receipt is confirmed.

Following this confirmation, one or more of the following activities may occur depending on the circumstances: recording which products were taken from storage, performing quality checks, and requesting the ordered products from inventory. Any combination of these three activities can be executed, and they must all complete before proceeding.

Once the applicable activities are finished, the process splits into two parallel paths that must both be completed. In one path, approval is obtained. In the other path, a packing slip is printed.

After the packing slip is printed, one or more of the following activities may take place: packaging the items securely, and printing an invoice. If an invoice is printed, the products are then measured. Both the secure packaging and the product measuring (if applicable) must complete before this branch can continue.

Once both the approval path and the packaging/invoicing path are complete, the process continues to examine other orders for potential delivery overlaps.

Finally, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

After confirming that payment has been received, one or more of the following activities may occur depending on the situation: recording which products were taken from storage, performing quality checks, and requesting the ordered products from inventory. Any combination of these three activities can be carried out as needed.

Once the applicable activities from the previous step are completed, the process splits into two parallel paths that must both be completed.

On the first path, a packing slip is printed. Following this, one or both of the next activities may take place: packaging the items securely and printing an invoice. If an invoice is printed, the products are then measured. Once the packaging and/or the measuring (if applicable) are complete, this path concludes.

On the second path, approval is obtained.

After both parallel paths are finished—meaning the approval has been obtained and the packaging/invoicing activities are complete—the process continues by examining other orders for potential delivery overlaps.

Finally, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

After determining value-increasing opportunities, the process splits into multiple parallel paths where one or more of the following activities may occur: recording whether or not the customer responded, giving them a call, and recording if they are willing to talk.

Along one of these paths, after recording whether or not the customer responded, the process splits again where both confirming the call date and time and sending them an email occur simultaneously. Once both of these activities are completed, they converge back together.

All the parallel paths then merge back together, and the process continues with identifying the root cause(s) of the problem. Next, ideas to increase value are described to the customer.

The process then splits again where one or more of the following activities take place: recording the customer's decision and thanking them for their time and feedback. Once these activities are completed, they converge, and the customer is asked if they have any other concerns.

Following this inquiry, the process splits into two simultaneous activities: noting down important learnings from the conversation and sending learnings to appropriate managers. Both of these activities must be completed before the process can proceed.

Once both learning-related activities are finished, the parallel paths merge, and the process concludes at the end event.

The process begins when documents are sent to the receiving department. Once received, a receiving report is created.

Following this, two activities occur simultaneously: errors are reported to the relevant team member, and a three-way match is double-checked. Both of these activities must be completed before the process continues.

After both the error reporting and the three-way match verification are finished, three activities are initiated in parallel: a voucher is created for the documents, the documents are stored in the paid invoice file, and the invoice is entered into the accounts payable account.

Once the voucher is created, two additional activities begin concurrently: dates are checked to avoid penalty charges, and the payment is scheduled. Both of these must be completed before proceeding.

The process concludes when all three parallel branches are complete—meaning the voucher-related activities (checking dates and scheduling payment), storing in the paid invoice file, and entering the invoice into accounts payable have all finished. At this point, the process ends.

Following the introduction, two activities occur simultaneously: the employee's workstation is prepared, and a benefits package is prepared. Both of these tasks must be completed before proceeding.

Once both the workstation and benefits package are ready, the process continues with two more parallel activities: a mentor is assigned to the new employee, and the employee is given a tour of the office. Both of these activities must be completed before moving forward.

After the mentor assignment and office tour are finished, approval is obtained.

Once approval is granted, two final activities begin in parallel: the long-term goals are explained to the employee, and the onboarding process is reviewed over the next 60 days. Both of these activities must be completed before the process concludes.

The process ends after the long-term goals have been explained and the onboarding review period is complete.

The process begins with making an introduction.

After the introduction, there is a decision point where the process may optionally proceed to get approval, or it may continue directly. If approval is sought, once it is obtained, the process converges and continues forward.

Next, the process splits into two parallel paths that must both be completed: laying out a timeline and stating the available resources. These two activities happen simultaneously.

Once both the timeline has been laid out and the available resources have been stated, the paths merge and a kickoff meeting is held.

Following the kickoff meeting, the process again splits into two parallel activities: keeping communication and recording KPIs. Both of these activities are carried out concurrently.

After both communication has been maintained and KPIs have been recorded, the parallel paths converge, and another decision point is reached. From here, one or both of the following activities may be performed: terminating contractors and evaluating project outcomes.

Once the selected activities from this decision point are completed, the paths merge together and the process comes to an end.

The process begins when an applicant starts a loan application.

First, the applicant fills in the employment information form. Following this, the borrower completes the loan application.

After the loan application is completed, two activities may occur simultaneously or in any combination: a written notice is given to the applicant, and the application is checked for completeness. When the written notice is given, the application is sent back to the applicant. These parallel paths then converge before proceeding.

Once both the notice has been sent back and the completeness check is finished, the underwriting process begins.

After the underwriting process starts, multiple actions can be taken concurrently or in any combination: the interest rate may be changed, the loan application may be approved, and the loan amount may be reduced. Any or all of these adjustments can occur depending on the underwriting assessment.

Once all necessary adjustments from the underwriting process are complete, the applicant receives the loan funds, and the process ends.

The process begins with preparing a summary of your content.

After the summary is prepared, multiple promotional activities can be pursued simultaneously or in various combinations. You may share the content on social media, and you may also comment on related blog posts.

Following commenting on related blog posts, additional options become available: you can post on related forums and groups, and you can deep-link to the content from older posts.

After posting on forums and groups, further parallel activities open up: you can perform outreach to relevant contacts, and you can repurpose your content into different formats.

Once the content has been repurposed, you have the option to post on Q&A sites and to pay for promotion. These promotional payment and Q&A posting activities then converge together.

The outreach efforts and the combined Q&A/paid promotion activities are then synchronized. This synchronization point also merges with the deep-linking activity from older posts.

Finally, the social media sharing activity and all the other promotional pathways converge together, and the process ends.

Throughout this process, the inclusive nature of the decision points means that any combination of the available promotional activities can be selected and executed, providing flexibility in how content promotion is approached.

The process begins at the start and the first step is to prepare a summary of your content.

After preparing the summary, the process branches into multiple parallel paths that can be executed in any combination. One path involves emailing your subscribers, while another path involves posting on related forums and groups.

Following the email to subscribers, the process branches again. One option is to comment on related blog posts, and another is to deep-link to the content from older posts.

After commenting on related blog posts, the process splits into three possible activities that can occur in any combination: posting on Q&A sites, submitting to link roundups, and reverse engineering your competition. Once any or all of these activities are completed, they converge together.

This convergence then merges with the path from deep-linking to older posts. Subsequently, this combined flow merges with the path from posting on related forums and groups.

Once all the selected paths have been completed and merged together, the process reaches its end.

If you comment on related blog posts, additional promotional activities become available. You can then pursue any combination of the following: post on Q&A sites, submit to link roundups, or reverse engineer your competition. Once any or all of these activities are completed, they converge back together.

This path then merges with the deep-linking activity. Subsequently, both the email-related activities and the forum posting activity converge together.

After all selected activities from both main branches are completed, the process ends.

Following the path where the completion time is defined, two activities are then performed in parallel: assessing if any steps are confusing and looking to see if the process can be simplified. Both must be completed before moving forward.

Meanwhile, after considering where bottlenecks occur, the process examines potentially wasteful steps.

Once the assessment of confusing steps and simplification opportunities are both complete, along with the completion of noting automatable steps and examining wasteful steps, all paths converge and the process continues to write the potential process improvements.

The written improvements are then submitted to get approval for processing improvements.

After approval is obtained, two activities happen simultaneously: determining what improvements should go forward and adding feedback on the updated process. Both activities must be completed before proceeding.

Once both are finished, the process splits again into two parallel activities: determining how the process will be monitored and communicating the process changes. Both of these must be completed.

When both monitoring determination and change communication are complete, the process reaches its end.

After the receiving report is created, several activities may occur depending on the circumstances. Errors may be reported to the relevant team member, the receiving report may be gathered, and the vendor's invoice may be gathered. Any combination of these activities can take place.

When the vendor's invoice is gathered, additional verification steps may follow. A three-way match may be double-checked, and confirmation that all documents have been amended may occur. Either or both of these activities can be performed. Once these verification activities are completed, they converge with the other paths.

After reporting errors to the relevant team member, gathering the receiving report, and completing any verification steps, all paths come together. At this point, three activities occur simultaneously: all documents are stamped, the documents are stored in the paid invoice file, and dates are checked to avoid penalty charges.

Following the stamping of all documents, a voucher is created for the documents. After storing in the paid invoice file, additional processing may occur where the invoice is entered into the accounts payable account and the payment is scheduled. Either or both of these activities can happen.

Once the voucher has been created, the invoice processing activities are completed, and the date checking is finished, all paths synchronize and the process comes to an end.

The process begins with recording basic details about the customer.

After this initial step, two parallel activities can be performed simultaneously: determining ways to increase value and identifying key points of value for the customer.

Following the first path, after determining ways to increase value, an analysis of how the customer uses the product is conducted. On the second path, after identifying key points of value, the impact of potential cancellation is quantified.

Once both the product usage analysis and the cancellation impact quantification are completed, the process continues with recording whether the customer is willing to talk further.

If they are willing to engage, the next step involves identifying the root cause or causes of the problem they are experiencing.

After understanding the root causes, three activities can be performed in parallel: describing ideas to increase value for the customer, presenting them with a special offer, and informing them of key metrics that demonstrate the value of the product.

Once all three of these engagement activities are completed, the customer is thanked for their time and feedback.

Following this, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns.

Finally, important learnings from the conversation are noted down, and the process concludes.

Following this, three activities occur simultaneously: grades are prepared for SSO, an exam assignment is selected, and score criteria are applied.

After the score criteria are applied, three more activities happen in parallel: the grades are calculated, the gradebook is imported, and special grades are applied to individuals.

Once all three of these activities are completed—calculating grades, importing the gradebook, and applying special grades—the process waits until the preparation of grades for SSO and the selection of the exam assignment are also finished.

When all five parallel branches have converged, three new activities begin concurrently: the grades summary is reviewed, the course summary is reviewed, and any changes are applied.

After all three review and adjustment activities are completed, the grades are recalculated.

Finally, the results are submitted to SSO, and the process ends.

The process begins with making an introduction for the new employee. Following this, the new employee discusses their role, goals, and projects with their supervisor.

After this discussion, two activities happen in parallel: training material is assigned to the new employee, and they are taken out to lunch.

Once the lunch outing is complete, three activities occur simultaneously: a welcoming ceremony is held, expectations are explained to the new employee, and they are given a tour of the office.

Following the welcoming ceremony, a mentor is assigned to the new employee. After expectations are explained, the new employee is inducted into the company culture. These three parallel paths—assigning a mentor, inducting into company culture, and touring the office—all converge together.

Once both the training material assignment and the convergence of the welcoming activities are complete, the new employee is assigned their first project.

After the first project is assigned, three activities begin in parallel: check-in meetings are planned, long-term goals are explained, and reading material for personal growth is provided.

Following the planning of check-in meetings, the new employee is encouraged to socially interact with the team. After reading material is provided, the onboarding process is reviewed over the next 60 days.

Finally, once the social interaction encouragement, the explanation of long-term goals, and the onboarding review are all complete, the process comes to an end.

The process begins when a customer cancellation case is initiated.

First, the basic details of the customer and their cancellation request are recorded. Following this, the impact of the cancellation is quantified to understand the business implications.

After assessing the impact, multiple outreach activities can occur simultaneously or in any combination: an email is sent to the customer, a call date and time is confirmed for a scheduled conversation, and/or the customer is given a call directly. When an email is sent, whether or not the customer responded is recorded. When a call is made, it is recorded if the customer is willing to talk. The call date and time confirmation also feeds into the next stage.

Once these outreach activities and their outcomes are documented, the reasons why the customer wants to leave are summarized. 

Following this summary, efforts to retain the customer proceed with one or both of the following approaches: ideas to increase value for the customer are described, and/or the customer is informed of key metrics demonstrating the value they receive from the service.

After these retention efforts are completed, the process continues with parallel closing activities: the customer is thanked for their time and feedback, and the customer's final decision regarding the cancellation is recorded.

Once both of these activities are finished, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns. Finally, important learnings from the conversation are noted down, and the process ends.

The process begins when an order is received.

First, the order details are recorded. Following this, two activities occur simultaneously: checking that the products are in stock, and recording which products were taken from storage.

After checking stock availability, the ordered products are requested from inventory. Meanwhile, after recording the products taken from storage, quality checks are performed on those items.

Once both the inventory request is fulfilled and the quality checks are completed, the process continues with one or more of the following activities: the items are packaged securely, and/or approval is obtained.

After approval is obtained, three activities happen in parallel: the packing slip is printed, the products are measured, and the shipping label is attached to the packaging. Once the shipping label is attached, the invoice is printed.

The process waits until the packing slip is printed, the products are measured, and the invoice is printed before continuing. Additionally, if items were packaged securely, this must also be completed before proceeding.

Once all these activities are finished, the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle. Finally, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

0.text:
The process begins when documents need to be processed for payment.

First, the documents are sent to the senior accountant in the relevant department. Following this, a receiving report is created.

After the receiving report is created, one or more parallel activities may occur: errors are reported to the relevant team member, and separately, confirmation is obtained that all documents have been amended. Once the documents are confirmed as amended, a three-way match is double-checked.

When either or both of these parallel paths complete—reporting errors and/or completing the three-way match verification—the process continues with another set of activities that may occur in parallel: the documents are stored in the paid invoice file, and a voucher is created for the documents.

After the documents are stored in the paid invoice file, additional parallel activities take place: the invoice is entered into the accounts payable account, and all documents are stamped.

Once the invoice entry and document stamping are complete, and also once the voucher creation is finished, all these paths converge and the process comes to an end.

Once the loan application is completed, three activities occur simultaneously: a written notice is given to the applicant, the application is sent back to the applicant, and the application is checked for completeness.

After all three of these activities are finished, the underwriting process begins.

Once the underwriting process is complete, three additional activities happen in parallel: the loan amount is reduced, the loan application is approved, and the interest rate is changed.

After all three of these activities are completed, the borrower receives the loan funds, and the process ends.

The process begins at the start event, after which the basic information is confirmed.

Following this confirmation, one or more paths may be taken: confirming if the process requires optimization and/or identifying the process's components. These activities can occur independently or together.

Once these initial assessments are complete, the process continues with one or more analysis activities: defining how long it takes to complete the process and/or looking to see if the process can be simplified. If simplification is explored, an assessment is then made to determine if any steps are confusing.

After these analysis activities converge, the potential process improvements are written. These documented improvements then go through an approval process for processing improvements.

Following approval, multiple activities may proceed: using the updated process, defining what would make the improvements successful, and/or determining what improvements should go forward. When the updated process is used, this leads to either updating the process documents and/or adding feedback on the updated process. Meanwhile, determining which improvements should proceed leads to choosing who will test the updated process.

Once all these parallel tracks converge, three activities occur simultaneously: determining how the process will be monitored, scheduling the next process review and optimization, and implementing the process changes.

After all three of these activities are completed, the process reaches its end.

The process begins with making an introduction for the new employee.

Following the introduction, two paths may proceed, with one or both being taken. On one path, the employee's workstation is prepared, after which the new hire discusses their role, goals, and projects with their supervisor. On the other path, a benefits package is prepared for the employee.

After the benefits package is prepared, one or both of the following activities may occur: accounts are created for the employee, and required reading materials are assigned. Once accounts are created, three activities happen simultaneously: employee paperwork is prepared, a job description with responsibilities is provided, and approval is obtained. All three of these must complete before proceeding.

The process then waits for the completion of both the reading materials assignment and the parallel administrative tasks, as well as the completion of the supervisor discussion from the other path. Once these converge, the process continues.

Next, one or more of the following activities take place: the new employee is taken out to lunch, training material is assigned, and they are inducted into the company culture. After whichever of these activities occur, the process moves forward.

Three activities then happen in parallel: the first project is assigned, approval is obtained again, and the paperwork is checked. All three must be completed before continuing.

Finally, two activities occur simultaneously: the onboarding process is reviewed over the next 60 days, and the new employee is encouraged to socially interact with the team. Once both of these are finished, the process ends.

Following this, two activities happen simultaneously: quality checks are performed, and which products were taken from storage is recorded.

After the quality checks are completed, two more activities occur in parallel: checking that the products are in stock and requesting the ordered products from inventory.

Once both the stock check and inventory request are finished, and the recording of products taken from storage is also complete, the process continues with two concurrent activities: printing a packing slip and printing an invoice.

After the packing slip is printed, three activities are carried out simultaneously: getting approval, packaging the items securely, and measuring the products.

When all three of these activities are completed, and the invoice printing is also finished, the process moves forward to a point where one or more of the following activities may be performed: loading items into the delivery vehicle, arranging the delivery, and examining other orders for delivery overlaps.

Once at least one of these delivery-related activities is completed, a confirmation email is sent to the customer.

The process ends after the confirmation email has been sent.

First, the order details are recorded. Following this, two activities happen simultaneously: quality checks are performed, and a record is made of which products were taken from storage.

After the quality checks are completed, two more activities occur in parallel: checking that the products are in stock and requesting the ordered products from inventory. Once both of these checks are complete, the process waits for the storage record to also be finished before proceeding.

Next, two activities run concurrently: printing the packing slip and printing the invoice. After the packing slip is printed, three activities begin in parallel: getting approval, packaging the items securely, and measuring the products. Once all three of these tasks are completed, the process waits for the invoice printing to also finish.

Following this synchronization point, one or more of the following activities may occur depending on the situation: loading items into the delivery vehicle, arranging the delivery, and examining other orders for delivery overlaps. Once the necessary delivery-related activities are completed, a confirmation email is sent to the customer.

The process ends after the confirmation email has been sent.

The process begins with learning how to identify future failures.

Following this, one or both of the following activities may be pursued: analyzing the specific product market share and making plans for future products. At least one of these must be completed before proceeding.

Once the selected market and product planning activities are finished, two activities occur simultaneously: reviewing the number of employees and reviewing the business plan.

After reviewing the business plan, one or more of the following reviews take place: reviewing enthusiasm, reviewing team chemistry, and reviewing expertise. At least one must be performed.

When the enthusiasm review is completed, three activities happen in parallel: reviewing employee salary and benefits, reviewing company mission and direction, and reviewing ability as a team leader.

After reviewing the ability as a team leader, two activities are conducted simultaneously: reviewing the relationship to the founder and reviewing trustworthiness. Both of these must be completed before moving forward.

The process then synchronizes at a point where the reviews of employee salary and benefits, company mission and direction, and the combined founder relationship and trustworthiness reviews all converge. Additionally, the team chemistry and expertise reviews must also complete and join at this convergence point, along with the earlier employee number review.

Once all these parallel review streams are synchronized, the process continues with one or both of the following financial checks: checking cash flow and checking the exit strategy. At least one must be selected.

If cash flow is checked, it is followed by checking current debt. If exit strategy is checked, it is followed by checking income statements. Once the selected financial paths are complete, the process converges.

The reputation of the competition is then analyzed, followed by checking insurance.

The process concludes after the insurance check is complete.

The process begins when an order is received and the order details are recorded.

Following this, two activities happen simultaneously: quality checks are performed, and the ordered products are requested from inventory. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

Once both the quality checks and inventory request are finished, three parallel activities begin: the items are packaged securely, the products are measured, and approval is obtained. These three activities can occur at the same time.

After the products are measured, two additional tasks are carried out in parallel: the shipping label is attached to the packaging, and a packing slip is printed. Both of these must be completed before moving forward.

The process then waits for all three parallel branches to complete—the secure packaging of items, the completion of the shipping label and packing slip tasks, and the approval—before continuing.

Once all these activities are finished, the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle.

Finally, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

The process begins at the start event and immediately proceeds to learning why startups fail so often.

After gaining this understanding, the process splits into two parallel paths that can be executed simultaneously. On one path, the product necessity is considered, while on the other path, the specific product market size is evaluated. Once one or both of these activities are completed, the paths converge.

Following this, the trustworthiness is reviewed. After this review, the process again branches into two parallel activities: checking cash flow and checking current debt. These financial assessments can occur concurrently. After one or both of these checks are finished, the paths merge back together.

The process then splits once more into two parallel activities focused on competitive analysis. On one path, the growth stage of competition is analyzed, while on the other path, the exact competition is identified. After completing one or both of these analyses, the paths converge again.

Finally, trademarks are checked, and the process concludes at the end event.

The process begins when a document is sent to the senior accountant in the department. Following this, a receiving report is created.

At this point, the process splits into two possible paths that may be taken based on certain conditions. In one path, the receiving report is gathered. In the other path, a three-way match is double-checked.

After the three-way match is verified, the process may branch into one or more of the following activities depending on the circumstances: gathering the vendor's invoice, confirming all documents have been amended, or reporting errors to the relevant team member. Once the receiving report has been gathered and any necessary activities from the three-way match verification have been completed, the paths merge together.

The process then splits into three parallel activities that must all be performed simultaneously: stamping all documents, scheduling the payment, and entering the invoice into the accounts payable account.

After all three of these activities are completed, the process concludes.

The process begins and the first step is to record basic details about the customer situation. Following this, key points of value are identified to understand what benefits the customer currently receives.

Next, whether or not the customer responded is recorded, and then a summary is created explaining why they want to leave.

At this point, two activities occur simultaneously: the customer is informed of key metrics demonstrating value, while at the same time ideas to increase value are described to them. Both of these activities must be completed before the process continues.

Once both value-related discussions are complete, one or both of the following activities may occur depending on the situation: the customer's decision is recorded, and/or they are thanked for their time and feedback. At least one of these must be performed, but both can be done.

After the applicable activities from the previous step are completed, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns. Finally, the learnings from this interaction are sent to appropriate managers, and the process ends.

The process begins at the start and proceeds with making an introduction.

Following the introduction, several activities can be performed in parallel or any combination thereof: identifying the approval status, getting approval, and recording the basic idea.

When getting approval is completed, the team works out its value. All the parallel branches—identifying the approval status, working out its value (which follows getting approval), and recording the basic idea—must complete before the process continues.

Once these activities converge, the team lays out a timeline. After the timeline is established, a kickoff meeting is held. Following the kickoff meeting, key performance indicators (KPIs) are recorded.

After recording the KPIs, the process splits again where some or all of the following activities occur: evaluating project outcomes and ensuring the project is completed.

When project outcomes are evaluated, contractors are terminated. Both the termination of contractors and ensuring the project is completed must finish before the process can conclude.

Once all closing activities are complete, the process reaches its end.

The process begins when documents are sent to the vendor accounting department. Following this, a receiving report is created.

At this point, two activities are performed in parallel: the vendor's invoice is gathered, and simultaneously, a three-way match is double-checked.

After the three-way match verification is complete, two more activities happen concurrently: the receiving report is gathered, and any errors are reported to the relevant team member. Once both of these activities are finished, they synchronize together.

The process then waits for both the vendor's invoice gathering and the error reporting/receiving report activities to complete before continuing.

Next, three activities are performed simultaneously: dates are checked to avoid penalty charges, the invoice is stored in the paid invoice file, and the invoice is entered into the accounts payable account.

After checking the dates, two more concurrent activities begin: a voucher is created for the documents, and all documents are stamped. Following the voucher creation, the payment is scheduled. Once the payment scheduling and document stamping are both complete, they synchronize.

Finally, the process waits for all three parallel branches (the voucher/stamping/payment branch, storing in the paid invoice file, and entering into accounts payable) to complete before the process ends.

First, the previous loan statement is provided to the lender. Following this, the borrower completes the loan application.

After the application is completed, one or more paths may be taken: the process may proceed directly forward, or the application may be sent back to the applicant for revisions. At this point, two activities occur simultaneously: the interest rate is changed, and the loan application is approved. Both of these activities must be completed before the process can continue.

The process begins when a target date for approval is set. Following this, two activities are carried out simultaneously: any significant variances are evaluated, and the most recent budget is reviewed. Once both of these activities are completed, three to five goals are prioritized.

Next, the average monthly cost is estimated. After this estimation is complete, two activities occur in parallel: all sources of income are listed, and total annual income is projected. When both of these income-related activities are finished, all financial data is recorded in a budget spreadsheet.

Finally, approval is obtained from top management, and the process comes to an end.

The process begins with preparing a summary of your content.

After the summary is prepared, there is a decision point where one or more paths may be taken. One option is to post on Q&A sites, and another option is to deep-link to the content from older posts. Either or both of these activities can be pursued.

If posting on Q&A sites is chosen, this is followed by submitting to link roundups.

If deep-linking to the content from older posts is chosen, this leads to a point where two activities must be performed simultaneously: emailing your subscribers and paying for promotion. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

Once both emailing subscribers and paying for promotion are finished, this path converges with the path from submitting to link roundups. When all pursued paths have completed, the process concludes and reaches its end.

On one path, approval is obtained, after which two activities happen simultaneously: the products are measured, and the items are packaged securely. The process begins with seeking pre-approval of final grades.

After obtaining pre-approval, the process branches into one or more parallel paths. The grades are calculated, and optionally, special grades may be applied to individuals.

Once the grades have been calculated, two activities occur simultaneously: preparing the grades for SSO and selecting the exam assignment. Both of these must be completed before proceeding.

After both preparing grades for SSO and selecting the exam assignment are finished, and if special grades were applied to individuals, the process converges before continuing.

The process then splits again into two parallel activities: applying any changes and reviewing the course summary. After applying any changes, the grades summary is reviewed. Once both the grades summary review and the course summary review are complete, the process converges.

Next, three activities are performed simultaneously: exporting the final grades, recalculating the grades, and exporting the course summary. All three must be completed before moving forward.

Once these exports and recalculation are finished, two final activities occur in parallel: sending the examiners grade approval sheet and submitting the results to SSO.

After both the grade approval sheet has been sent to examiners and the results have been submitted to SSO, the process concludes and reaches its end.

After obtaining pre-approval, the process branches into one or more parallel paths. The grades are calculated, and optionally, special grades may be applied to individuals.

Once the grades are calculated, two activities occur simultaneously: the grades are prepared for SSO, and an exam assignment is selected. Both of these tasks must be completed before proceeding.

After these parallel activities converge, and once any special grades have also been applied (if that path was taken), the process continues with another set of parallel activities. Any changes are applied while simultaneously the course summary is reviewed.

Following the application of changes, the grades summary is reviewed. Once both the grades summary review and the course summary review are complete, the process moves forward.

At this point, three activities are performed concurrently: the final grades are exported, the grades are recalculated, and the course summary is exported. All three of these tasks must be finished before the process can continue.

Once these exports and recalculation are complete, two final activities occur in parallel: the examiners grade approval sheet is sent, and the results are submitted to SSO. After both of these activities are completed, the process ends.

The process begins with the creation of a purchase requisition.

Once the requisition is created, approval is sought from one or both of two sources: the finance team and the manager. These approvals can be obtained independently or together, depending on the requirements.

After the necessary approvals have been received, two activities happen simultaneously: the purchase order is created, and the supplier is informed that the order is ready for approval.

Once both of these activities are completed, approval is obtained from the supplier.

Following the supplier's approval, two activities occur in parallel: the delivery date is confirmed, and the details are sent to the department.

After both the delivery date confirmation and the communication of details to the department are complete, the process comes to an end.

The process begins with recording basic details.

Following this, one or both of the following activities may occur: reviewing the most recent budget and evaluating any significant variances. Once the selected activities are completed, the process continues.

Next, one or both of these activities may be performed: determining ways of achieving the goals, or defining three to five goals followed by prioritizing those three to five goals. After the chosen path or paths are completed, the process moves forward.

Subsequently, one or both of the following may take place: listing all department expenses and estimating the average monthly cost. Once these activities are finished as needed, the total annual income is projected.

After projecting the annual income, two activities occur simultaneously: recording financial data in a budget spreadsheet and finalizing the budget. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

Once both are done, one or both of the following activities may occur: requesting approval from top management and obtaining approval from top management. After the necessary approval activities are completed, the process ends.

Following this, the process branches into one or more parallel paths: reviewing the most recent budget and evaluating any significant variances. Either or both of these activities may be performed depending on the circumstances.

Once the applicable review activities are completed, the process again splits into optional parallel paths: determining ways of achieving the goals, and defining three to five goals. If goals are defined, they are then prioritized.

After these goal-related activities converge, the process branches once more into optional parallel activities: listing all department expenses and estimating the average monthly cost. One or both may be completed as needed.

When these expense-related activities are finished, the total annual income is projected.

Following this projection, two activities must be completed simultaneously: recording financial data in a budget spreadsheet and finalizing the budget. Both of these activities are mandatory and occur in parallel.

Once both the financial recording and budget finalization are complete, the process splits into optional paths for the approval phase: requesting approval from top management and obtaining approval from top management. Either or both of these approval activities may occur.

When the applicable approval activities are completed, the process concludes and ends.

The process begins with recording basic details.

After this initial step, there is an opportunity to review the most recent budget and/or evaluate any significant variances. These activities may be performed together, individually, or one of them may be skipped depending on the circumstances.

Once the review and evaluation activities are completed, the process moves forward to goal setting. Here, ways of achieving the goals may be determined and/or three to five goals may be defined. If goals are defined, they are then prioritized. These goal-related activities can occur in various combinations based on what is needed.

Following the goal-setting phase, the process continues with expense and cost analysis. Department expenses may be listed and/or the average monthly cost may be estimated. Again, these activities can be performed together or selectively.

After addressing expenses and costs, the total annual income is projected.

Next, two activities occur simultaneously: the financial data is recorded in a budget spreadsheet, and the budget is finalized. Both of these tasks must be completed before proceeding.

Once both the spreadsheet recording and budget finalization are done, the process moves to the approval phase. Here, approval from top management is requested and/or obtained. These approval-related activities may happen in combination as appropriate.

The process concludes once the approval activities are completed.

The process begins when a borrower initiates a loan application.

First, the borrower provides the bank statement to the lender. Following this, one or more of the following activities may occur: the application is received by the credit department, and/or the borrower completes the loan application. Once at least one of these activities is completed, the process continues.

Next, two activities occur simultaneously: the application is sent back to the applicant, and a written notice is given to the applicant. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

After both notifications are handled, one or more of the following activities may take place: the underwriting process begins, and/or the credit score and risk score are checked. Once at least one of these evaluations is completed, the process moves forward.

Based on the assessment results, one or more adjustments may be made: the interest rate may be changed, and/or the loan amount may be reduced. After at least one of these modifications is finalized, the borrower receives the loan funds, and the process concludes.

The process begins when the borrower provides the bank statement to the lender.

Following this, one or more of the following activities may occur: the application is received by the credit department, and/or the borrower completes the loan application. Once at least one of these activities is completed, the process continues.

Next, two activities happen simultaneously: the application is sent back to the applicant, and a written notice is given to the applicant. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

After both activities are finished, one or more of the following may take place: the underwriting process begins, and/or the credit score and risk score are checked. Once at least one of these activities is completed, the process moves forward.

Subsequently, one or more adjustments may be made: the interest rate may be changed, and/or the loan amount may be reduced. After at least one of these adjustments is completed, the borrower receives the loan funds, and the process ends.

Once the purchase requisition is created, two activities occur simultaneously: approval is obtained from the finance team, and approval is obtained from the manager. Both approvals must be completed before proceeding.

After both approvals are received, two activities are initiated in parallel: the purchase order is created, and the supplier is informed that the order is ready for approval. Both of these activities must be completed before moving forward.

Once both the purchase order creation and supplier notification are finished, approval is obtained from the supplier.

Following the supplier's approval, two activities begin concurrently: the purchase order is filed, and the delivery date is confirmed.

After the purchase order is filed, two more activities run in parallel: details are sent to the department, and the purchase order is recorded. Both of these activities must be completed.

Finally, the process waits for all parallel activities to conclude—sending details to the department, recording the purchase order, and confirming the delivery date—before the process comes to an end.

The process begins with making an introduction for the new employee.

Following the introduction, two activities happen simultaneously: accounts are created for the new employee, and approval is obtained.

Once both the account creation and approval are complete, three activities begin in parallel: the office is toured, a welcoming ceremony is held, and a mentor is assigned.

After a mentor is assigned, three more activities occur concurrently: expectations are explained to the new employee, they are inducted into the company culture, and training material is assigned.

Once the expectations have been explained, the company culture induction is complete, and the training material has been assigned, these activities converge. This convergence then joins with the completion of the office tour and the welcoming ceremony.

After all these parallel activities are finished, two more tasks happen simultaneously: approval is obtained again, and the paperwork is checked.

Once both the approval and paperwork check are complete, the process continues with one or more of the following activities that may occur based on certain conditions: the long-term goals are explained, the onboarding process is reviewed over the next 60 days, and the new employee is encouraged to socially interact with the team.

When the applicable activities from this set are completed, the process concludes and ends.

The process begins at the start event and proceeds with recording the buyer's details.

Following this, two paths may be taken simultaneously or individually. On one path, the buyer is sent the terms of sale, after which approval for post-credit check review is obtained. On the other path, a credit application form is sent to the buyer, followed by running a credit check on the purchasing company.

Once one or both of these paths are completed, the process converges and then splits again into two possible concurrent activities. On one path, customer payment terms are checked, and then the invoice is sent using accounting software. On the other path, the invoice is generated directly.

After one or both of these invoice-related paths are completed, a second physical copy is made. The sales on credit of services are then recorded, and the process concludes at the end event.

1.text:
The process begins when it is initiated at the start point.

First, the buyer's details are recorded. Following this, two activities may occur in parallel or selectively: the terms of sale are sent to the buyer, and a credit application form is sent to the buyer.

After the terms of sale are sent, approval for a post-credit check review is obtained. Simultaneously, after the credit application form is sent, a credit check is run on the purchasing company.

Once both the approval for the post-credit check review is obtained and the credit check on the purchasing company is completed (or at least one of these, depending on which paths were taken), the process continues.

The process begins with making an introduction for the new employee.

Following the introduction, two activities occur simultaneously: providing a job description with responsibilities, and preparing the employee's workstation. Both of these must be completed before proceeding.

Once the job description has been provided and the workstation is ready, two more activities happen in parallel: assigning a mentor to the new employee, and taking them out to lunch. Both activities must be finished before moving forward.

After the mentor has been assigned and the lunch has taken place, two activities are carried out concurrently: getting approval and assigning the first project to the employee. Both of these need to be completed before continuing.

Once approval has been obtained and the first project has been assigned, two final parallel activities begin: encouraging the new employee to socially interact with the team, and providing reading material for personal growth. The reading material activity is followed by reviewing the onboarding process over the next 60 days.

After both the social interaction encouragement and the onboarding review have been completed, the process comes to an end.

The process begins with having an onboarding call with the client.

Following the onboarding call, three activities are carried out simultaneously: creating a first draft of the marketing plan, updating the project management profile, and scheduling future calls.

After creating the first draft, approval is obtained for it. Meanwhile, after updating the project management profile, campaign ideas are researched.

Once approval for the first draft has been obtained, campaign ideas have been researched, and future calls have been scheduled, the client is informed of the project start.

After informing the client, one or both of the following activities may occur: making changes based on a follow-up call, or sending a post-onboarding survey. If a post-onboarding survey is sent, a follow-up call takes place afterward.

Once the necessary activities are completed—either making changes based on the follow-up call, having the follow-up call after the survey, or both—the process concludes.

The process begins with recording the buyer's details.

Following this, three activities occur simultaneously: getting approval for a post-credit check review, sending a credit application form to the buyer, and sending the buyer the terms of sale. After sending the terms of sale, a credit check is run on the purchasing company.

Once all three parallel paths are completed—the approval is obtained, the credit application form is sent, and the credit check is finished—the process continues with another set of three simultaneous activities: generating the invoice, sending the invoice in the accounting software, and checking customer payment terms.

After all three of these activities are completed, the process proceeds to a point where one or more of the following may occur: recording the activity digitally or making a second physical copy. If the activity is recorded digitally, monthly contact with the client is then established. Once the digital recording and monthly contact are complete (if applicable), and the second physical copy is made (if applicable), these paths converge.

The process then continues to another point where one or more of the following may take place: recording the sales on credit of services or recording the sales on credit of goods. After whichever of these recording activities are completed, they converge and the process ends.

The process begins with recording the customer's basic details.

Following this, three activities are performed simultaneously: analyzing how the customer uses your product, determining ways to increase value for them, and identifying key points of value. After analyzing product usage, the impact of potential cancellation is quantified. Once all three parallel paths are completed—quantifying cancellation impact, determining ways to increase value, and identifying key points of value—the process continues.

Next, two activities happen in parallel: confirming the call date and time, and giving the customer a call. After confirming the call date and time, one or both of the following may occur: recording whether or not the customer responded, and recording if they are willing to talk. If the customer's response is recorded, an email is sent to them. Once the email-related activities and the willingness-to-talk recording are completed, and after the call has been made, the process proceeds.

At this point, one or both of the following activities may take place: summarizing why the customer wants to leave, and asking open-ended questions. After these activities are completed, three actions are performed simultaneously: describing ideas to increase value, presenting the customer with a special offer, and informing them of key metrics demonstrating value.

Once all three persuasion activities are finished, one or both of the following occur: thanking the customer for their time and feedback, and recording the customer's decision. After these are completed, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns. Finally, important learnings from the conversation are noted down, and the process ends.

After the exit strategy and cash flow checks are completed, two activities are performed in parallel: analyzing the reputation of competition and identifying the exact competition. Once both competition-related activities are finished, trademarks are checked.

The process begins when a support ticket arrives and needs to be handled.

First, the ticket type is checked to understand what kind of inquiry has been received.

Based on the initial assessment, the process branches into multiple possible paths that can be followed simultaneously or selectively. The ticket may be determined to be a 'Marketing/PR Question' and/or a 'Technical Issue'.

If the ticket is identified as a Marketing/PR Question, the process continues where it may additionally be classified as a 'Feature Request' and/or an "I'm not sure question".

When the ticket is identified as an "I'm not sure question", two parallel activities occur simultaneously: the ticket is classified as an 'App Question' and also as a 'Mixed-type question'. Both of these classifications must be completed before proceeding.

Once the App Question and Mixed-type question determinations are finished, and the Feature Request determination is also complete (if applicable), these paths converge.

Similarly, when the ticket has been determined to be a Technical Issue, this path joins with the other completed classifications.

After all applicable ticket type determinations have been made and synchronized, three activities are initiated in parallel: the issue is replicated, the ticket question is responded to, and technical issues are tested. All three of these activities must be completed.

Once the issue has been replicated, the ticket question has been responded to, and the technical issues have been tested, all parallel paths converge and the process comes to an end.

The process begins with making an introduction.

Following the introduction, two activities occur simultaneously: identifying the approval status and getting approval. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

Once both the approval status has been identified and approval has been obtained, a project plan is drawn up. After the project plan is completed, a kickoff meeting is held.

After the kickoff meeting, two activities run in parallel: recording KPIs and keeping communication. Both of these must be completed before moving forward.

Once both KPIs have been recorded and communication has been maintained, the process reaches a decision point where one or more of the following paths may be taken: terminating contractors or ensuring the project is completed.

If contractors are terminated, the project outcomes are then evaluated. After evaluating project outcomes, this path converges with the other path.

If ensuring the project is completed is chosen, this path proceeds directly to the convergence point.

Once one or both of the paths (evaluating project outcomes after terminating contractors, and/or ensuring the project is completed) have finished, the process concludes and reaches its end.

The process begins with entering results in the canvas gradebook.

Following this, one or more of the following activities may occur in parallel: the gradebook is imported, an exam assignment is selected, and special grades are applied to individuals. If the gradebook is imported, the grades are then calculated.

Once some or all of these parallel activities are completed, the grades summary is reviewed.

After reviewing the grades summary, one or both of the following activities may take place: the course summary is exported and the final grades are exported. If the course summary is exported, the grades are then recalculated.

When some or all of these export activities are finished, the process continues with one or both of the following activities occurring in parallel: approval signatures are obtained from the course director, and results are submitted to SSO. If results are submitted to SSO, the examiners grade approval sheet is then sent.

Once some or all of these final activities are completed, the process ends.

After entering the results, one or more of the following activities may occur in parallel: the gradebook is imported, the exam assignment is selected, and special grades are applied to individuals.

Once the gradebook has been imported, the grades are calculated. When the grade calculation is complete, along with the completion of selecting the exam assignment and applying special grades (whichever paths were taken), a review of the grades summary takes place.

Following the grades summary review, the process splits again where the course summary may be exported and/or the final grades may be exported. If the course summary is exported, the grades are then recalculated. After recalculating the grades and/or exporting the final grades, the paths converge.

The process then splits once more into parallel activities: approval signatures are obtained from the course director, and results are submitted to the SSO. After submitting results to the SSO, the examiners grade approval sheet is sent.

Once the approval signatures have been obtained and the examiners grade approval sheet has been sent, all paths converge and the process ends.

First, the results are entered in the Canvas gradebook. Following this entry, multiple activities can occur in parallel: the gradebook is imported, the exam assignment is selected, and special grades are applied to individuals as needed.

After importing the gradebook, the grades are calculated. Once the grade calculation is complete, along with the exam assignment selection and application of special grades, the grades summary is reviewed.

After reviewing the grades summary, two activities can proceed simultaneously: the course summary is exported, and the final grades are exported. When the course summary has been exported, the grades are recalculated. Once both the grade recalculation and the final grades export are complete, the process continues.

At this point, two parallel activities begin: approval signatures are obtained from the course director, and the results are submitted to SSO. After submitting the results to SSO, the examiners grade approval sheet is sent.

First, the results are entered in the Canvas gradebook. Following this entry, several activities can occur in parallel: the gradebook is imported, the exam assignment is selected, and special grades are applied to individual students as needed.

Once the gradebook has been imported, the grades are calculated. After the grade calculation is complete, along with the exam assignment selection and the application of special grades, the grades summary is reviewed.

Following the review, two activities can proceed concurrently: the course summary is exported, and the final grades are exported. After exporting the course summary, the grades are recalculated. Once both the grade recalculation and the final grades export are complete, the process continues.

At this point, two parallel activities begin: approval signatures are obtained from the course director, and the results are submitted to the SSO (Student Services Office). After submitting the results to the SSO, the examiners grade approval sheet is sent out.

Once both the course director's approval signatures have been obtained and the examiners grade approval sheet has been sent, the process concludes.

The process begins with making an introduction.

Following the introduction, two activities occur in parallel: recording the basic idea and identifying the approval status.

After identifying the approval status, one or both of the following activities may take place depending on the conditions: working out its value and getting approval. Once the required activities from this set are completed, the process continues.

When both recording the basic idea is finished and the approval-related activities are completed, three activities commence simultaneously: laying out a timeline, drawing up a project plan, and setting a budget.

After drawing up a project plan, the available resources are stated. Once the timeline is laid out, the available resources are stated, and the budget is set, all three parallel paths converge.

A kickoff meeting is then held, followed by recording KPIs.

After recording KPIs, two activities happen in parallel: evaluating project outcomes and ensuring the project is completed.

Following the evaluation of project outcomes, contractors are terminated. Once both the contractors are terminated and the project completion is ensured, the process concludes and ends.

The process begins at the start event.

First, there is a focus on learning how to identify future failures, followed by gathering specific product details.

After obtaining the product details, the process branches into multiple optional paths that can be taken individually or in combination. These paths involve reviewing team chemistry, reviewing ability as a team leader, and reviewing the number of employees. Once any or all of these team-related reviews are completed, the paths converge.

The process then branches again into multiple optional paths for financial analysis. These include checking cash flow, checking income statements, and checking the exit strategy. When checking income statements, the process further splits into two parallel activities that must both be completed: checking current debt and checking quarterly projections. After both of these are finished, they merge back together. All the financial analysis paths then converge once the selected activities are completed.

Following the financial review, the process branches once more into optional paths for market and competition analysis. One path involves projecting the market share, which leads to knowing the exact competition. Another path involves analyzing the reputation of the competition, which leads to analyzing the growth stage of the competition. After these competition-related activities are completed, the paths merge together.

The process then splits again into optional paths for compliance verification, which include checking insurance and checking patents. Once any or all of these compliance checks are completed, the paths converge, and the process concludes at the end event.

Following this, one or both of the next activities may occur: thanking the customer for their time and feedback, and recording the customer's decision. At least one of these must be completed, but both may be performed depending on the situation.

After these activities conclude, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns.

Once this conversation wraps up, two activities happen in parallel: sending the learnings to appropriate managers, and noting down important learnings from the conversation. Both of these must be completed.

The process ends after both the learnings have been documented and shared with the relevant managers.
